definitions.explanation: External shutters on traditional Japanese houses that slide along tracks to protect windows from rain, storms, and intruders.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}が{来|く}るので{雨戸|あまど}を{閉|し}めた。
examples.english: I closed the storm shutters because a typhoon is coming.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}になったら{雨戸|あまど}を{開|あ}ける。
examples.english: Open the storm shutters when morning comes.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{家|いえ}には{木製|もくせい}の{雨戸|あまど}がある。
examples.english: Old houses have wooden storm shutters.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE: Traditional Japanese houses have {雨戸|あまど} that slide horizontally on tracks outside the windows. They are closed at night and during storms.

FUNCTIONS:
・Protection from rain and wind
・Security (closed at night)
・Insulation (keeps cold out)
・Privacy

MODERN VERSIONS:
・Electric/motorized shutters
・Roll-up shutters (シャッター)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{雨戸|あまど}を{開|あ}ける (to open shutters)
・{雨戸|あまど}を{閉|し}める (to close shutters)
・{雨戸|あまど}を{立|た}てる (to put up shutters)
